document.title: Transcript of Telephone Conversation Between Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin and Afghan Prime Minister Nur Mohammed Taraki, March 18, 1979
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan: Lessons from the Last War
document.note: Kosygin tells Taraki the USSR will not send troops and urges him to rely on the local population, including mobilizing industrial workers in Herat province. This shows Soviet misunderstanding of local conditions. Source: CWIHP Bulletin 8-9, pp. 145-146.

mentions.quote: Kosygin: We have decided to quickly deliver military equipment and property to you and to repair helicopters and aircraft.
At the Central Committee Politburo's sitting on 19 March, Comrade Kosygin read the transcript of these conversations
Taraki: We ask that you extend practical and technical assistance, involving people and arms.
Why can't the Soviet Union send Uzbeks, Tajiks, and Turkmens in civilian clothing?

events.description: Telephone conversation in which Taraki asks Kosygin for Soviet people and arms, including troops in Afghan uniform, to retake Herat; Kosygin declines overt intervention but promises equipment, repairs, grain and price changes.
Politburo sitting where Kosygin read the transcript in the presence of Central Committee secretaries.

Telephone conversation between Kosygin and Taraki on the Herat revolt; Taraki requests Soviet troops, tanks, aircraft and crews in Afghan markings or civilian clothing; Kosygin declines to commit and promises consultations.
Soviet decision to deliver military equipment free of charge, repair helicopters and aircraft, deliver 100,000 tons of grain and raise gas prices from $21 to $37.
Taraki urges a decisive attack on Herat against the rebels.
Central Committee Politburo sitting at which Kosygin read the transcript to Central Committee secretaries.

relationships.detail: Kosygin and Taraki discussed Soviet military assistance and the Herat uprising in a telephone conversation.
relationships.quote: Transcript of Telephone Conversation Between Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin and Afghan Prime Minister Nur Mohammed Tarki, 17 or 18 March 1979

relationships.detail: Taraki is Afghan Prime Minister, speaking for the government.
relationships.quote: Afghan Prime Minister Nur Mohammed Tarki

relationships.detail: Kosygin is Soviet Premier and speaks for the Soviet decision to supply aid.
relationships.quote: We have decided to quickly deliver military equipment and property to you and to repair helicopters and aircraft.

relationships.detail: The Afghan government is to receive Soviet military equipment, repairs and grain free of charge. Direction is recipient to provider, so Afghan Government is funded by Soviet Government.
relationships.quote: All this is for free. We have also decided to deliver to you 100,000 tons of grain

relationships.quote: All this is for free. We have also decided to deliver to you 100,000 tons of grain

sources_cited: Moscow Russian Television Network in Russian, "Special File" program
key_claims: Taraki tells Kosygin the Herat population is almost wholly under the influence of Shiite slogans and gives no active support to the government.
Taraki claims most Soviet-trained Afghan officers are 'Moslem reactionaries' who cannot be relied upon.
Taraki asks Kosygin to send Soviet Uzbeks, Tajiks and Turkmens in Afghan uniforms with Afghan-marked tanks and aircraft to attack Herat.
Kosygin refuses concealed intervention, warning the world would learn of it within two hours, but promises free military equipment, aircraft repairs, 100,000 tons of grain and a gas price increase.
Taraki accuses Iran and Pakistan of coordinated action against the Afghan government.
Kosygin proposes exploiting Iranian hostility to the United States for propaganda and contact with Iran's progressives.
